name: eMudhra Ltd
title: eMudhra Ltd - 543533 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Software/PKI firm, not a capital-cycle story: FY26 PAT ₹1,100m (+26%) with FY27 guided at 18% top line and 25–30% PAT growth, but Q4 PAT rose only 21.6% and no capacity discipline is discussed.

summary.headline: eMudhra FY26 total income rose 35.1% to INR 7,132 million and PAT 26.2% to INR 1,100 million; FY27 guided to 18% top-line and 27-28% PAT growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR 1,966 million (+31.7% YoY) and PAT was INR 296 million (+21.6% YoY, 15.1% margin). For FY26, Enterprise Solutions and Services revenue was INR 5,616 million and Trust Services INR 1,400 million, with EBITDA up 32.6% to INR 1,654 million. Management guided FY27 organic top-line growth of about 18% and PAT growth of 25-30%, with an ambition to double PAT in three years. Q4 India enterprise revenue declined QoQ, which management attributed to a larger Q3 defence deal.

financial_highlights.change: Enterprise Solutions grew 55% YoY (23% organic, 32% acquisitive)

segments.name: Enterprise Solutions
segments.commentary: 59% of revenue; grew 55% YoY in FY26 (23% organic, 32% acquisitive). CertiNext (CLM) and SecurePass (IAM) added accounts across financial services, government, energy and education. India enterprise grew 27.6% for FY26 despite a Q4 dip.

segments.name: Trust Services
segments.commentary: About 20% of revenue; grew 32% YoY in FY26, mainly India, driven by combo certificates, tokens sold via portal, and eSign. Management expects about 20% growth in FY27.

segments.name: Pure Services
segments.commentary: About 21% of revenue; flat YoY. Management expects no growth in FY27, in line with industry trends.

segments.name: US Products
segments.commentary: Product revenue rose from about USD 6.5-7 million to more than USD 9.5 million. Management expects 25-30% growth next year, aided by a large TLS order from the InCommon university consortium (about 700 universities).

guidance_outlook: FY27 organic top-line growth of about 18% (management said 15-18% base range, 'most likely 18%').
FY27 PAT growth of about 25-30%, with a point estimate of 27-28%; ambition to double PAT over three years.
Product-led growth: Enterprise Solutions expected to grow 25-30% in FY27, with services flat and Trust Services about 20%.
Order book projected at 2.2x-2.3x the prior-year level, with some Middle East orders delayed by the conflict that began in February.
Cryptas expected to contribute over USD 1 million of profit in FY27, dependent on replacing the incumbent US CLM vendor.
capex_capacity: Data centres operating in the US, Europe, UAE and India to meet data-sovereignty requirements.
Invested in senior US management and a US data centre, which management says is beginning to yield results.
No new product acquisition in the pipeline; any AI-cybersecurity bolt-on would most likely be US-based and could come in Q3 or Q4 FY27.
demand_pricing: Order book disclosed as INR 238 crore (product business only, excluding services).
Management said it does not disclose individual deal values.
Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) POCs are underway, mainly in BFSI and defence, with some closed-user-group deployments possible in FY27. Regulatory timelines point to 2029-2030.
Europe demand is driven by NIS2 and DORA. Cryptas sales cycles are long because customers are large banks.
Africa DPI pipeline (digital ID, PKI, e-passports, e-sign) is at advanced stages; Middle East and APAC pipelines are also progressing.
Revenue model unchanged: products on recurring billing and licence; services exposure is limited to about 20-21% of revenue.
Google root certificate transition: existing roots remain trusted until new roots are accepted. Management sees no current impact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Google's root certificate policy change and its effect on US products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no real deadline; new roots were submitted earlier and existing roots keep working until Google accepts the new ones, so there is no impact for now.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 238 crore order book product-only, and how is US products growth expected to look?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, product only. Management expects 25-30% US product growth next year, aided by the InCommon order, and says the order book is projected at 2.2-2.3x.

qa_highlights.question: Will Enterprise and Services growth meet the guidance given the cybersecurity tailwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it guides conservatively. Services will show no growth, Trust Services about 20%, and the balance from enterprise products at 25-30%. Revenue is recognised only on execution, which takes time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India enterprise revenue fall in Q4, and what is driving trust services growth?
qa_highlights.answer: India enterprise grew 27.6% for FY26; Q3 had a larger defence deal, so Q4 looks lower. Trust Services growth came from partner-led combo certificates, token sales, retail, and eSign.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the 3i Infotech dispute?
qa_highlights.answer: No police complaint or SEBI inquiry has been received. eMudhra sent a legal notice to 3i Infotech and its directors and is awaiting a reply; nothing has moved in two months.

qa_highlights.question: What is Cryptas' FY26 contribution and profitability outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Cryptas revenue was about INR 85 crore for the year, with roughly break-even to USD 1-2 crore... specifically about INR 1-2 crore total profit. 8-9 conversations are underway to replace an incumbent US CLM product with CertiNext.

risks_watch: Middle East order delays linked to the conflict that began in February 2026.
Dispute with 3i Infotech: legal notice sent, no resolution yet.
Long European sales cycles for Cryptas CLM replacement; profit uplift depends on displacing the incumbent.
Revenue recognition depends on execution timing for large bank and government orders, which may lag bookings.
Q4 India enterprise decline; quarterly lumpiness from large deals.
Competitive and product-positioning questions on AI-driven threats (Anthropic Mythos) and PQC deployment timing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and the FY27 product-led thesis, but deliberately conservative on guidance, saying past guidance has been met and they avoid overestimating. Evasive on deal sizes and on the 3i Infotech dispute, where they said nothing has progressed.
key_quotes: FY2026 was a year of compounding momentum for us.
Over a 5-year horizon, we have compounded PAT at 30.5% per annum.
No, we always want to estimate in a reasonable way and then think that under almost, if you see last 4-5 years, whatever guidance we have given, we have achieved 100%.
Our ambition is to double PAT over the next 3 years.

growth.why: FY27 organic revenue growth guided at about 18% (15-18% range, most likely 18%) and PAT growth 25-30% (point 27-28%), backed by a disclosed INR 238 crore product order book and projected 2.2-2.3x order book, though no specific capacity additions were described and Middle East orders are delayed.
